# CLI reference

> **Audience:** deck authors, agents and contributors · **Generated from:** src/cli/*.ts · **Version:** 0.7.6

Run from a clone with `node dist/slidecraft.mjs <command>` (zero install) or `npx tsx src/cli/main.ts <command>` during development. Every command accepts `--json`; when stdout is not a terminal, commands with structured results print JSON (the others ignore the flag and print plain text).

## `rebuild`

Rebuild an original native PPTX through shared geometry into editable PPTX and HTML

```
Usage: slidecraft slidecraft rebuild [options] <pptx>

Rebuild an original native PPTX through shared geometry into editable PPTX and
HTML

Arguments:
  pptx                 authoritative original PowerPoint

Options:
  -o, --out <dir>      output directory; original is never overwritten
  -f, --format <list>  comma-separated: pptx,html,pdf,png (default: "pptx,html")
  --pdf-engine <id>    native | html | pptx-convert
  --png-engine <id>    resvg | pptx-convert
  --json               machine-readable output
  -h, --help           display help for command
```

## `visual-qa`

Final LLM review stage: render through PowerPoint and Chrome, write a review pack (images, differences, measured facts); --record stores the reviewer findings and a user report

```
Usage: slidecraft slidecraft visual-qa [options] <deck>

Final LLM review stage: render through PowerPoint and Chrome, write a review
pack (images, differences, measured facts); --record stores the reviewer
findings and a user report

Arguments:
  deck                      deck.yaml

Options:
  -o, --out <dir>           build output directory (default: <deck dir>/dist)
  --width <px>              raster width (default: "1600")
  --record <findings.json>  append a review round and rewrite
                            visual-qa/REPORT.md
  --json                    machine-readable output
  -h, --help                display help for command
```

## `build`

Build the deck into PPTX / PDF / PNG / HTML

```
Usage: slidecraft slidecraft build [options] <deck>

Build the deck into PPTX / PDF / PNG / HTML

Arguments:
  deck                  path to deck.yaml

Options:
  -f, --format <list>   comma-separated: pptx,pdf,png,html,onepager,docx
  --pptx-engine <id>    auto | pptxgenjs | artifact-tool
  --pdf-engine <id>     auto | native | html | pptx-convert
  --png-engine <id>     auto | resvg (Scene preview) | pptx-convert (actual
                        Office render)
  -o, --out <dir>       output directory (default: <deck dir>/dist)
  --preview-width <px>  PNG preview width
  --json                machine-readable output
  -h, --help            display help for command
```

```

Arguments:
```

## `theme from`

Create a theme from a sample: a reference PDF, a screenshot (PNG/JPEG) or a website — colours, fonts and margins

```
Usage: slidecraft slidecraft theme from [options] <sample>

Create a theme from a sample: a reference PDF, a screenshot (PNG/JPEG) or a
website — colours, fonts and margins

Arguments:
  sample                 PDF, PNG/JPEG file or http(s) URL

Options:
  --id <id>              theme id (kebab-case)
  --name <name>          display name
  -o, --out <dir>        output folder (default: "slidecraft-theme")
  --font-dir <dir>       folder with the font files (TTF/OTF) to measure them
                         exactly
  --heading-font <name>  heading font, when the sample has none (pictures)
  --body-font <name>     body font, when the sample has none (pictures)
  --json                 machine-readable output
  -h, --help             display help for command
```

## `import`

Import an existing .pptx into a draft deck.yaml (text, tables, charts, images, notes)

```
Usage: slidecraft slidecraft import [options] <file>

Import an existing .pptx into a draft deck.yaml (text, tables, charts, images,
notes)

Arguments:
  file               the presentation to import

Options:
  -o, --out <dir>    output folder (default: ./slidecraft/<file-name>)
  --id <id>          deck id
  --theme <id|path>  theme for the draft (default: "consulting-classic")
  --render           also render the original to original.pdf
                     (PowerPoint/LibreOffice) for a visual redesign pass
  --json             machine-readable output
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

## `sync`

Bring text edited in PowerPoint (or Keynote, Google Slides) back into deck.yaml, field by field

```
Usage: slidecraft slidecraft sync [options] <deck> <pptx>

Bring text edited in PowerPoint (or Keynote, Google Slides) back into deck.yaml,
field by field

Arguments:
  deck        path to deck.yaml
  pptx        the edited .pptx (built by SlideCraft, then edited)

Options:
  --apply     write the changes into the YAML (comments kept) and re-check
  --json      machine-readable output
  -h, --help  display help for command
```

## `images`

Fill empty image slots: generate pictures for imagePrompt (OpenAI-compatible API), or find licensed stock photos for imageQuery (--stock)

```
Usage: slidecraft slidecraft images [options] <deck>

Fill empty image slots: generate pictures for imagePrompt (OpenAI-compatible
API), or find licensed stock photos for imageQuery (--stock)

Arguments:
  deck                path to deck.yaml

Options:
  --dry-run           list the prompts or searches that would be sent; send
                      nothing
  --force             replace images that already exist
  --stock [provider]  stock photos for imageQuery: auto (default: Openverse +
                      Wikimedia Commons, no key), openverse, wikimedia, pexels
                      (PEXELS_API_KEY), pixabay (PIXABAY_API_KEY)
  --list              with --stock: show candidate photos (title, author,
                      licence, link); download nothing
  --pick <n>          with --stock: take the n-th candidate from --list
                      (default: 1)
  --json              machine-readable output
  -h, --help          display help for command
```
